<reason>A genuinely close, high-quality debate. CON (A) built a sharp incumbency/patronage attack ("who picks the explorers?", "a pension indexed to whoever won last") and a strong "second door / which system finds its errors" weighing frame. But PRO (B) kept the motion's actual trade in focus: accountability cost is conceded by the proposition, so the question is whether the extra "prophecy gate" aids discovery. PRO's A1 distinction between backward-looking judgment of records and forward-looking prediction of untested bets squarely answered CON's best pressure question, and its "third gate" framing showed CON's system runs the same peer committees plus an added filter that rewards preliminary data. PRO also effectively turned Karikó: public competition rejected her for a decade and the rescuing door (industry) exists under either system, undercutting CON's pluralism argument. CON's late "institutional averages/purge before review day" mechanism was clever and only partly answered, and PRO's clipped rebuttal is a small execution cost, but PRO's core thesis remained cleaner and more decisive at the end.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's A1 in Rebuttal 2 ([B4.1]-[B4.2]): answering CON's "why trust peers to spot daring people but not daring ideas" by distinguishing retrospective assessment of demonstrated records from consensus prediction of untested bets, and noting CON's system runs both filters anyway. It neutralized CON's sharpest pressure question and set up the "what does the extra gate buy" closing frame.</best_rebuttal>
